title: Response Variance Lens — wireframes and walkthrough
content:
Purpose and high-level idea:

This is an exploratory design for a "Response Variance Lens" — a compact debugging view in the Console that helps engineers and product owners quickly understand when generated responses vary across otherwise-identical calls (same prompt, model, parameters) and when variance correlates with errors (timeouts, 5xx, model errors, hallucinations). The lens is intentionally compact so it can be embedded as a flyout from a call detail, or pinned as a secondary pane next to the existing timeline/trace view.

Goals:
- Surface distributions of outputs for repeated calls (token-level variance, top-k differences, length variance)
- Highlight anomalies where variance spikes around errors / high latency / repeated 5xx
- Provide fast investigative actions: compare runs, copy canonical prompt, pin a run, re-run with deterministic flags, route to fallback model
- Keep the UX light-weight for SREs and engineers who need to triage quickly during incidents

Target users and scenarios:
- Platform SRE during an outage: want to know whether model nondeterminism is a contributor to inconsistent client behavior
- Product engineer debugging a customer report that “sometimes the model returns unrelated answers”
- Solutions engineer validating that a canary model rollout introduced regressions (spike in variance + higher 5xx)

Key components (wireframe text descriptions):

1) Mini-summary bar (top) — compact metrics
- Call sample: N = 14 (number of repeat-executions captured in selected time window)
- Variance score: 0.42 (0–1, aggregated metric combining token-level entropy, edit distance, and top-token divergence)
- Error overlay: 3 timeouts, 1 5xx, 2 model-error-outputs (tagged)
- Quick actions: [Re-run pinned] [Set deterministic=true] [Compare top-2 runs] [Route to fallback]

UX notes: the variance score should be computed server-side and cached; show a tooltip explaining its composition. Quick actions should trigger small confirm overlays (re-run) or open a compare panel (compare).

2) Strand view (middle) — compact visual representation of each captured response as a horizontal band (like transcription lanes)
- Each lane shows: response length (bar), token-density heatstrip (hot segments where tokens differ vs canonical), error glyphs near the right edge (timeout, 5xx icons)
- Hovering a lane shows inline tokens (first 280 characters) and a copy button
- Lanes are sorted by similarity to the modal/canonical run (highest similarity at top)

Wireframe note: lanes should be visually compact (32–40px height) to fit many samples; color-coded chips indicate error type and whether the run used a fallback model or different routing policy.

3) Delta overlay (right side) — compare two selected runs side-by-side
- Synchronous token-level diff with inline annotations: dropped tokens, inserted tokens highlighted
- Token-level confidence / logprob bar below each token if available (from model metadata)
- Accept/Reject checklist for triage: "Is variance acceptable?" "Is it correlated to latency?" "Recommend: re-run, pin, rollout rollback"

Interaction notes: selecting two runs should animate the diff and pin the selection for subsequent steps (e.g., create an incident note with both runs attached). Support keyboard shortcuts (j/k to move selection).

4) Correlation strip (bottom) — small sparkline matrix mapping variance to other signals across time
- Rows: variance_score, p95 latency, p99 latency, #timeouts, #5xx, error-rate
- Time granularity: selectable (1m/5m/1h)
- Clicking a cell/timepoint filters the strands to only runs inside that window

Backlog grooming items (prioritized):
- M1: Server-side variance scorer implementation + API returning sample runs (JIRA-RT-541)
- M2: Basic strand view + mini-summary bar; implement quick actions: re-run + deterministic toggle
- M3: Delta overlay (token diff) with logprob bars (requires enriched token metadata pipeline)
- M4: Correlation strip — hook into metrics store to fetch latency/error counts per time bucket
- M5: Incident export — ability to attach selected runs and a short triage note to a generated incident record

Acceptance criteria (for MVP - M1+M2):
- Console surface shows variance lens flyout from any call detail
- Lens shows at least N=5 sample runs and computes a variance score
- Strand view renders lanes for each run and indicates error glyphs
- Quick action "Re-run pinned" triggers a re-run API call and displays new run in the lens
- Performance: lens renders within 350ms for up to 25 samples (client-side rendering budget)

Edge cases and UX decisions:
- Low-sample: If fewer than 3 captured runs exist, show guidance: "Recording more calls increases confidence — enable sampling for this route." Provide a one-click toggle to enable sampling at 1%/5%/10%
- Privacy: redaction rules should apply — any PHI or customer identifiers must be masked in the inline tokens. The lens should honor existing data retention and redaction policies from Private deployments
- Mixed-model runs: If runs come from different model variants (rollout or fallback), show a model chip and allow filtering to only same-model runs
- Deterministic flag: UI must warn when re-running with deterministic to avoid masking nondeterminism bugs in prod

Accessibility and triage flows:
- Provide text-only export of the lens contents for inclusion in incident emails
- Keyboard navigable lanes and actions; provide ARIA labels for error glyphs

Mockup copy and microcopy suggestions:
- Variance score tooltip: "A combined measure of how different the responses were across captured runs. Higher values mean more variability. Computed from token entropy, normalized edit distance, and top-token KL divergence."
- Error glyph hover: show full error message + request id + region + model variant
- Quick action confirmation: "Re-run pinned? This will issue a fresh request with the same prompt and parameters. Use deterministic to pin RNG seeds (may hide nondeterministic issues)."

Developer notes / implementation hints:
- Add field to events: sample_bucket_id and sample_group_id to batch related runs; this simplifies retrieval for the lens
- Server API: GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/variance?window=1h&limit=25 -> returns variance_score, run_summaries[] (id, length, error_tags, model_variant, token_snippet, timestamp)
- Token metadata pipeline: if logprobs enabled, persist top-k tokens with logprobs (configurable sampling to bound storage)
- Client: use virtualized list for strand view to keep rendering costs low for many samples

Future / nice-to-have ideas (post-MVP):
- Auto-root-cause suggestion: use heuristics to surface likely causes (e.g., variance spikes right after a model rollout, or correlated with spike in queue time)
- Integrate with Evaluate: automatically run a batch evaluator on pinned runs to compute QA metrics
- Acceptable variance policy: let product teams set thresholds and receive alerts when variance > threshold for a route

Open questions (for PM/Eng discussion):
- How often should we sample runs for high-traffic routes without excessive storage cost? (1% seems reasonable but needs experimentation)
- What is the canonical composition of the variance_score? Are teams likely to want tunable weighting between edit distance and token entropy?
- Should we store token-level logprobs by default for all customers, or provide as an opt-in feature?

Next steps / meeting asks:
- Review API contract with backend infra (Marco) — can we augment call events with sample_group ids?
- Engineering sync to scope M1 and M2 for an 8-week sprint (Priya to own backlog)
- Design review for strand visual (Diego to prepare polished mocks with color accessibility checks)

Notes to include in PRD draft:
- Keep lens embeddable and optional — it should not be enabled by default for all customers
- Provide admin control for sampling and token metadata retention policies
- Expose quick triage actions in Console and via the SDK (so SREs can re-run from CLI)

Appendix: quick ASCII wireframe (for devs/designers)
[Top bar] | N=14 | Variance: 0.42 | 3 timeouts | 1 5xx | [actions]
[Strand lanes: ]
> lane 1: [|||||||||||||||||............] (no error)
> lane 2: [|||||||||---|||-------] (timeout glyph)
> lane 3: [|||||||||||||||||] (fallback model chip)
[Delta overlay] | run A vs run D diff (highlighted tokens)
[Correlation strip] | variance ▓▓▓░░ | p95 ▓░░ | timeouts ░░▓ |  

End of doc."
